products.name: Upvas Bhajani Pith
products.description: Upvas Bhajani Pith, also known simply as Bhajani or Upvas Bhajani, is a special flour mixture used in Indian cuisine, particularly in the state of Maharashtra. It is primarily prepared for fasting or upvas, during religious festivals or specific fasting days, when certain grains and ingredients are restricted. Upvas Bhajani Pith is a versatile mix used to make various fasting dishes. The composition of Upvas Bhajani Pith can vary, but it typically includes a combination of flours and grains that are allowed during fasting periods, such as water chestnut flour (singhare ka atta), rajgira flour (amaranth flour), sama rice flour (barnyard millet), sabudana (tapioca pearls), and other ingredients like cumin seeds, salt, and sometimes groundnut flour. To prepare dishes with Upvas Bhajani Pith, you can make a dough or batter by mixing it with water and then use it to create various fasting-friendly foods like thalipeeth (pancakes), bhajani chakli (a type of snack), and other treats. These dishes are suitable for those observing fasts and dietary restrictions as they do not contain grains like wheat, rice, or pulses. Upvas Bhajani Pith is an essential ingredient for making these fasting dishes and adds flavor and texture to the recipes while adhering to the dietary guidelines.

products.description: Khapravarchi / Khandeshi Puran Poli – Smoky, Traditional & Flavor-Packed ( खापरावरची / खान्देशी पुरणपोळी – पारंपरिक चव आणि खमंग धूरकट वासाने भरलेली ) Experience the authentic taste of rural Maharashtra with Khapravarchi Puran Poli , a beloved version of the classic sweet flatbread cooked on a clay pot lid ( khapar ) for a smoky and earthy aroma . This Khandeshi specialty is especially prepared during festivals like Holi, Diwali, and Padwa , and is known for its unique cooking style and rich flavor. Key Ingredients (साहित्य): Chana Dal (चना डाळ) – Base of the sweet stuffing Gul (गूळ) & Sakhar (साखर) – Natural sweetness Velchi (वेलची) & Jayfal (जायफळ) – Traditional spices Maida (मैदा) or Gahu (गव्हाचे पीठ) – Soft dough for rolling Tel / Tupa (तेल / तूप) – For softness and roasting Khapar (खापर) – Earthen lid adds signature smoky flavor How It’s Made (कशी बनवतात): The chana dal is cooked and blended with jaggery, sugar, cardamom, and nutmeg to create the puran. The outer dough is rolled thin and stuffed generously. Unlike regular puran poli, this version is roasted on an inverted clay lid over open flame , which gives it a slightly crisp texture and smoky aroma , making it truly rustic and traditional. Serving Suggestions: Serve it hot with a dollop of homemade ghee , warm milk , or a side of katachi amti (कटाची आमटी). Each bite brings nostalgia and warmth from Khandesh’s kitchens. products.description: Puran Poli – Simple, Sweet & Soft ( पुरणपोळी – पारंपरिक गोड चव) Puran Poli is the most popular and classic version of Puran Poli in Maharashtra . It’s a soft, sweet flatbread made by stuffing a rich filling of chana dal, jaggery, cardamom, and nutmeg inside a wheat flour dough, then roasted on a tawa with ghee or oil. Prepared especially during festivals like Holi , Diwali , and Gudi Padwa , it’s a comforting traditional dish loved by all generations. Key Ingredients (साहित्य): Chana Dal (चना डाळ) Gul (गूळ) Velchi (वेलची) Jayfal (जायफळ) Gahu Peeth / Maida (गव्हाचे पीठ / मैदा) Tup / Tel (तूप / तेल) Serving Suggestions: Serve hot with homemade ghee, warm milk, or katachi amti.

products.description: Kokani Puran Poli – Coconut-Infused Sweet Delight (कोकणी पुरणपोळी – गोड नारळाच्या चवेसह) Hailing from the Konkan region of Maharashtra, Kokani Puran Poli adds a delicious coastal twist to the classic recipe. products.description: Vidarbha Puran Poli – Rich, Flavorful & Traditional (विदर्भी पुरणपोळी – पारंपरिक आणि खमंग) A delightful traditional sweet flatbread known for its rich and smooth filling, Vidarbha-Style Puran Poli is cherished during festivals like Holi, Diwali, and Padwa . The puran (sweet filling) is crafted with care using cooked chana dal blended with jaggery and sugar, flavored with aromatic cardamom (velchi) and nutmeg (jayfal). Wrapped in a soft dough of wheat flour or maida, each poli is roasted with ghee or oil for a golden finish and melt-in-the-mouth texture. Key Ingredients (साहित्य): Chana Dal (चना डाळ) Gul (गूळ) Sakhar (साखर) Velchi (वेलची) Jayfal (जायफळ) Maida / Wheat Flour (गव्हाचे पीठ / मैदा) Tup / Sunflower Oil (तूप / तेल) How It’s Made: The chana dal is cooked till soft and mashed, combined with jaggery, sugar, cardamom, and nutmeg to make the puran. The dough is prepared with flour and oil, rolled out, stuffed with puran, and gently roasted on a tawa with ghee or oil until golden brown. Serving Suggestions: Serve hot with a dollop of homemade ghee, warm milk, or traditional katachi amti (spiced dal water). Each bite delivers a perfect balance of sweetness and softness, ideal for festive celebrations.

products.name: Shingada Shevaya
products.description: "Shingada Shevaya" is a popular Indian dish. It is often referred to as "Singhare ki Sevai" or "Water Chestnut Noodles." This dish is commonly prepared during fasting periods, particularly in India, and is suitable for people who observe specific dietary restrictions during those times. The primary ingredient in Shingada Shevaya is singhara flour (water chestnut flour), which is used to make thin noodles or vermicelli. These noodles are cooked with various ingredients such as ghee (clarified butter), spices, peanuts, and sometimes vegetables or herbs, depending on personal preferences and regional variations. Shingada Shevaya is enjoyed for its mild, nutty flavor and is a suitable option for those who avoid grains like wheat and rice during their fasting period. It can be seasoned with rock salt and other permissible fasting spices to add flavor while adhering to dietary restrictions. Overall, Shingada Shevaya is a delightful and satiating dish that provides a unique culinary experience during fasting or vrat (religious observance) days.

products.name: Shingada Chivda
products.description: Shingada Chivda, also known as Singhara Chivda, is a popular Indian snack typically made during fasting periods when certain dietary restrictions are followed. It is a delicious and crunchy snack that doesn't contain grains like wheat or rice, making it suitable for those who are observing fasting rituals or have gluten-free dietary requirements. The main ingredient in Shingada Chivda is water chestnut flour (singhare ka atta), which is mixed with various other ingredients. Common additions include peanuts, dry fruits, raisins, and spices like cumin seeds, green chilies, and rock salt (sendha namak), as regular salt is usually avoided during fasting. The mixture is then shallow-fried or roasted until it's crispy and golden brown. Shingada Chivda is known for its savory and slightly spicy flavor, as well as its satisfying crunch. It is enjoyed as a snack during fasting days or as an accompaniment to tea or other beverages. This snack is not only delicious but also provides energy and nutrition when fasting, making it a popular choice for those observing fasting rituals in India.

products.name: Rajgira Pith
products.description: Rajgira Pith, also known as Rajgira Pitha or Rajgira Ke Laddu, is a traditional Indian sweet treat made from Rajgira flour, which is also known as amaranth flour. It is a popular dish, especially during festivals and fasting periods when grains like wheat are avoided. To prepare Rajgira Pith, Rajgira flour is roasted in ghee (clarified butter) to enhance its flavor and then mixed with sugar or jaggery, along with other ingredients such as desiccated coconut, cardamom powder, and chopped nuts. The mixture is then shaped into small, round laddus or balls. The result is a sweet, nutty, and delicious treat that's enjoyed for its unique taste and nutritional benefits. Rajgira is highly nutritious and rich in protein, making Rajgira Pith a popular choice for those following a vegetarian or fasting diet. These laddus are often offered as prasad (an offering to deities) during religious rituals and are relished as a sweet snack by people of all ages.

products.name: Rukhvat
products.description: In some cultures, particularly in South Asian countries like India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh, a 'sugar rukhwat' is a traditional gift exchange or display of sweets and gifts presented during weddings, engagements, or other significant ceremonies. The term "sugar" refers to the sweet treats and delicacies that are typically included in these displays, while "rukhwat" means a gift or offering. The sugar rukhwat often comprises an elaborate arrangement of various sweets, fruits, nuts, and other edible items, beautifully presented on decorative trays or platters. These sweets may include traditional favorites such as ladoos (sweet balls made of flour, sugar, and ghee), barfis (sweet fudges made from condensed milk), jalebis (deep-fried pretzel-like sweets soaked in sugar syrup), and more. In addition to the sweets, the sugar rukhwat may also feature other gifts such as jewelry, clothing, accessories, or household items, depending on the customs and preferences of the families involved. The presentation of the sugar rukhwat is often considered an important aspect of the ceremony, symbolizing hospitality, generosity, and the celebration of the occasion. It serves as a token of appreciation and respect between the families involved and is meant to enhance the joyous atmosphere of the event.
